newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close higher on budget prospects.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close higher on budget prospects.

text.p: Delhi shares reversed early losses and closed higher on Monday, boosted by Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's statement that he wanted the 1997/98 (April-March) budget passed, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 10.50 points higher at 792.54. It was 3.01 points down in afternoon trade.
"Expectations that the budget will be passed by the new govrnment generated a buying spree towards the later part of the session," said Sanjay Mittal of brokers S.R.M. Securities.

Lower house speaker P.A. Sangma told reporters after a meeting with Gujral that the prime minister wanted to push through the budget that outgoing Finance Minister P. Chidambaram presented to parliament on February 28.
State Bank of India firmed 7.10 rupees at 311.25.
Oriental Bank of Commerce gained 0.25 rupee at 79.
Larsen and Toubro gained four rupees to 229.
